invariants: Listing forwards the exact caller signal to the currently mounted persistence provider, and checks abort before and after listing.
Listing failures retain the literal source message and original Error or foreign rejection value as cause; cancellation preserves the exact signal reason.
Live records win after the persistence listing and retain persisted availability; immutable header mismatches identify the precise session.
Duplicate durable records use the final occurrence; cloned output does not mutate live metadata and selected ASCII identities retain newest-first tie ordering.

Twelve fresh actual corpus/SessionStore observations and seventy unchanged source baseline assertions execute from the pinned source; actual JSONL/SQLite regressions refuse pre-abort before touching the backend.
identity: Session id, original failure/cause and signal identity, exact cloned header, live/persisted availability and runtime import root are retained.
ownership: The query lists once and owns detached output headers; persistence owns backend enumeration, which must not begin for an already aborted signal.
ordering: Abort precedes backend access; durable duplicate resolution precedes the current live overlay; conflict checking precedes publishing that overlay.
errors: Literal source name/code/message and cause/failure identity are frozen, including unknown foreign rejection values.
cancellation: Optional signal extends the public Python persistence.list interface compatibly for ordinary callers; owned providers check before and during enumeration.
adaptation: ThrownValueError carries a JavaScript non-Error rejection. Only tested ASCII tie ordering is covered; full locale collation is unverified.
open_questions: Clean complete gate and actual extracted acceptance pending. Full corpus exact reads, bounded concurrent title folding, FTS, long history, arbitrary locale sorting, Web/profile journeys and deferred Win7 remain outside this contract.
